# QC01: 绮春园宫门 Qichun Yuan Gongmen

Wave 4 · Qichun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=QC01` · Page: `/scenes/#QC01` · Row: `research/buildings/QC01-qichun-yuan-gongmen/`

## What it was

绮春园宫门 Qichun Yuan Gongmen, the main gate in the south of Qichun Yuan. Jiaqing ordered in 1808 a south-facing gate with offices, a screen wall and barriers on the model of the Changchun Yuan gate (E0566); it was built in 1809 and called the new gate (新宫门) (E0568, E0497). The gate quarter, from the screen wall to the hill behind 中和堂, measures about 200 by 120 m; the great and second gates are gate halls with rolled-ridge hip-and-gable roofs (E0568). It burned in October 1860 (E0680; E0497 lists the gate district among survivors, unverified). Malone's plate shows a gate rebuilt after 1860 by the empress dowager and the garden renamed 万春园 (E0492).

From the inventory row: **built** 嘉庆十四年 1809, 新宫门 (S49 lead); 嘉庆十四年 1809 (with 勤政殿 = QC02's predecessor name, to be checked); **destroyed** survived 1860 (S06;S49); 同治 repairs; ruined later; rebuilt 1988 (S57) (S49, S02, S06, S57, S01, S220).

## What survives today

The gates and walls were rebuilt on their sites in 1986 (E0568, S227) and serve as the park's south entrance (P0418, P0419, P0466, P0467): a modern rebuild, not the gate of 1860.

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.
